name: ChannelSpec
description:
ChannelSpec defines the configurable properties of a channel.

 The fields every type shares come first: which agent serves the channel,
 whether serving is enabled, which vaults supply the agent's tool
 credentials, and the per-turn run settings. The type, exactly one of
 web, slack or whatsapp, carries what only that type declares.

fields.name: AgentRef
fields.description:
Reference to the agent this channel serves.

 The referenced agent must live in this channel's organization: a
 channel offers an agent its own organization owns, billed to that
 organization, with tool credentials bound from it. To offer another
 organization's agent, install the plugin that carries it and make a
 channel for the installed copy.

 A version on the reference (a tag or a content hash) is the version
 each new conversation on this channel runs; none, or "latest", runs the
 agent's current version when the conversation starts. A started
 conversation keeps the version it started on.

 The agent cannot be changed after the channel is created.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.description:
Whether serving on this channel is enabled.

 Disabling is a configuration-preserving pause: a web channel keeps its
 origins, messages, credentials and link token, and its chat link
 answers NOT_FOUND; a Slack or WhatsApp channel keeps its install and
 credentials, and refuses inbound messages. Delete the channel instead
 for a full teardown.

fields.name: Vaults
fields.description:
Vaults whose logins and secrets this channel's conversations use, in
 order: the first vault holding a match wins. At most 20.

 This is how a tool-using agent becomes reachable over a channel: attach
 a shared vault holding the needed keys (for example a read-only API
 token). A channel's runs have no person of their own, so they use only
 these vaults, never anyone's My vault, and a My vault cannot be
 attached. A web channel takes vaults only when its audience is public:
 members chatting on an organization link use their own vaults.

fields.name: RunConfig
fields.description:
Per-turn model choice and run bounds for this channel's conversations.

 These settings are the turn's own layer: unset fields fall to the
 agent's defaults, then to the platform's channel or guest execution
 profile (RunConfig has the rule). A choice set here wins over the
 agent's; max_cost_usd and max_tool_rounds can only lower the agent's
 and the platform's caps, so a channel's owner can reduce what one turn
 may spend, never raise it. What a sender's own request carries is
 never read. A web channel takes run settings only when its audience is
 public.

fields.name: Web
fields.description: A hosted chat link and the chat widget other sites embed.

fields.name: Whatsapp
fields.description: A WhatsApp Business number connection (Meta Cloud API).
